cases.title: CDRENUMBER: No changes nothing in the Pit Schedule, Yes renumbers P9 -> P8 and P10 -> P9 only (non-P marks untouched), and U puts every schedule cell back exactly
cases.plan_item: UX-CPLAN-18/19 CDRENUMBER, whole card (daily card D20)
cases.expected: On the untouched copy: CDRENUMBER answered C1 then No prints the preview 'P9 -> P8' and 'P10 -> P9' and 'Renumber cancelled - nothing changed.', and the Pit Schedule read afterwards equals the schedule read before, cell for cell. CDRENUMBER answered C1 then Yes prints the same preview and 'Renumbered 2 pit(s) downhill to uphill. One Undo restores the old numbers.'; the schedule then lists P1 to P7, P8 and P9 (both 450 x 450) and C1, no P10, and the AGI, WT10, WT11 and WT12 sub-rows and the C1 row are still there. Two U (PITSCHEDULE, then CDRENUMBER) and every schedule cell equals the schedule before.
cases.why_not_unit: The network walk runs on the real drawing's pits and pipes and writes every label in one live command; the schedule is read from the live drawing.
not_automated: The PIT LABEL blocks on the plan are not read one by one (their handles are not known); the Pit Schedule rows stand for them. A TG mark is not in the recorded rows, so it is not checked.
Whether the network order chosen is the right engineering order is Tim's word (the numbering rule itself).
